title: Office Rental Costs in Midrand: Build Your Occupancy Budget
seoTitle: Office Rental Costs in Midrand: Budget Guide
seoDescription: Build an office budget using published Midpoint examples. Separate base rent, services, parking, deposits and fit-out before requesting a full quote.
excerpt: Budget for office occupation using dated unit examples, clear base-rent calculations and a checklist of recurring and initial costs.
contentHtml:
Build an office budget from the space your team needs, the agreed area and rate, and the charges and work required to occupy it. An advertised rental per square metre is a starting figure, not a complete monthly bill.

This guide supports our offices to rent in Midrand guide. Use it to prepare a budget before asking for a written, unit-specific quote.

Start with a dated base-rent calculation

For an area-based rental, multiply the agreed rentable area by the agreed monthly rate per square metre. Keep the measurement basis and VAT treatment attached to that calculation.

For example, the Sunbird ground-floor office listing, checked on 19 October 2026, publishes 500.66 m² at R120 per m² per month. Multiplication gives an indicative base rental of R60,079.20 per month. It does not establish an all-inclusive quote, confirm VAT treatment or guarantee that the unit is still available.

A second published example is Unit 1, 1 Weaver Avenue: 266 m² at R105 per m² per month, giving R27,930 in indicative monthly base rent. These are different spaces, not evidence of a market average or a like-for-like price comparison.

Separate recurring charges from move-in costs

Ask the leasing team to identify each applicable item as included, separately charged, metered, once-off or not applicable. A blank line is an unanswered question, not a zero cost.

  • Recurring occupancy: base rent, applicable recoveries, utilities, parking, connectivity and any separately charged services.
  • Initial cash requirements: deposit or other agreed security, any advance amounts, relocation, fit-out, furniture and connection costs.
  • Future commitments: agreed escalation dates, maintenance responsibilities, changes in service use and any end-of-occupation work described in the proposed lease.

Do not assume a deposit amount, escalation percentage or landlord contribution. Obtain those figures for the selected unit and proposed term. Read the written terms with your own advisers where needed.

Budget for the workplace you will actually use

The right office area depends on your layout, staff attendance, private rooms, meeting needs, storage and circulation. A larger floor plate is not automatically more economical because its advertised rate is lower. Use a current floor plan to test how much of the space serves your brief.

Check what is already fitted and what must change. Furniture, reception, meeting rooms, cabling and equipment may create different costs in two offices with similar advertised areas. The floor-plan and fit-out checklist helps turn those questions into a scope of work.

Compare a conventional office with a serviced option

If you are considering OnPoint, compare a written package against the conventional-office budget using the same team size and service requirements. Advertised meeting rooms, furniture options or tenant credits do not establish unlimited or included use. See our serviced versus conventional office comparison.

Keep the quote and the live schedule together

Use the live office comparison and current office vacancies for the latest published entries. An advertised date or “Immediately” remains subject to leasing confirmation. Listing photographs can show proposed works and do not replace a viewing.

If your requirement also includes warehousing, keep the budgets separate until the areas and scope are agreed. 2 Kingfisher remains flagged because its numeric area is 3,849 m² while its description states 3,300 m²; do not use it as a monthly-rent example until reconciled.

Next, use the office quote-comparison worksheet, or request an office quote and viewing with your team brief, preferred date and budget.

title: How to Compare Office Rental Quotes in Midrand
seoTitle: Compare Office Rental Quotes in Midrand
seoDescription: Compare office quotes on the same area, term, services and fit-out basis. Use a practical worksheet and current Midpoint office listings.
excerpt: Use the same area, charge, work and timing worksheet for each office quote, with unresolved figures kept visible.
contentHtml:
Compare office quotes using the same area basis, occupation date, lease period and workplace requirements. Two rates per square metre cannot tell you which office costs less to occupy if the quotes include different things.

Start with our Midrand office leasing guide and use this worksheet when you have a shortlist. For an initial budget, read the office rental cost guide.

Give each quote a clear identity

Record the building and unit, quote date, expiry or validity conditions, contact, advertised area and the proposed occupation date. Attach the plan or area schedule used for pricing. Confirm whether that area includes any shared or ancillary space rather than assuming every square metre is desk space.

For a dated source example, Unit 2, 2 Weaver Avenue published 1,614.7 m² at R120 per m² per month when checked on 19 October 2026. That gives R193,764 in indicative monthly base rent. The calculation does not settle VAT, recoveries, services, fit-out or handover.

Complete the same six lines for every option

  1. Area and base rent: record the agreed rentable area, measurement basis, rate per m² per month and resulting monthly amount. Flag any mismatch between the plan, schedule and quote.
  2. Recurring charges: list recoveries, utilities, parking, connectivity and other services. Mark whether each is included, separately priced, metered or awaiting confirmation.
  3. Initial payments: record the proposed deposit/security, advance payments and connection or setup charges, using the written offer rather than an assumed standard.
  4. Work and equipment: identify landlord and tenant work, furniture, cabling, equipment and relocation costs. Record any proposed contribution with its conditions.
  5. Timing: show the occupation date, required work, approvals, access for fit-out and when each quoted charge begins.
  6. Changes over the term: record agreed escalation dates, service limits, maintenance responsibilities and any reinstatement scope in the proposed terms.

Use consistent arithmetic

Keep recurring monthly costs, once-off spending and refundable security in separate columns. Adding a deposit to monthly rent obscures the cash timing; excluding fit-out spending can obscure the upfront requirement. Where a charge is unknown, leave it visibly unresolved and request clarification.

For a period comparison, use the proposed monthly amounts for each month, reflecting any agreed changes at the correct dates. Do not multiply the opening rent by the whole term if the written proposal changes that figure later. Compare VAT on the same stated basis and have the treatment confirmed.

Test whether both quotes solve the same problem

A quote for a space with fitted meeting rooms may require a different scope from a largely open floor plate. The cheaper opening rent may come with work your team has not budgeted for. Use the viewing checklist and floor-plan checklist to identify those differences.

If one option is serviced, use a package inclusion checklist as well. A serviced label does not establish what furniture, meeting use, connectivity or parking is included in the figure you were given.

Resolve inconsistent figures before choosing

Request a revised written quote where the area, rate, monthly amount or works scope conflicts. Arithmetic can reveal a mismatch but cannot establish which underlying figure is correct. For example, the warehouse/conversion listing at 2 Kingfisher remains flagged at 3,849 versus 3,300 m²; it is excluded from numeric rent examples until approved area and quote details agree.

Check the live office vacancies, then ask leasing for comparable written office quotes. Include your preferred units, occupation date, layout needs and parking requirement.

title: Serviced vs Conventional Offices in Midrand
seoTitle: Serviced vs Conventional Offices in Midrand
seoDescription: Compare serviced and conventional offices by layout, services, responsibilities and full cost. Explore current Midpoint and OnPoint listings.
excerpt: Compare the two leasing formats against one team brief, with dated OnPoint and conventional-office examples and clear package questions.
contentHtml:
Choose between a serviced and conventional office by comparing the workspace, services, responsibilities and written terms your team needs. The labels alone do not establish a total cost, a short lease or a ready-to-use fit-out.

This article supports our OnPoint serviced-office guide and links to the conventional office guide. Midpoint publishes both leasing formats in Halfway House, Midrand; confirm the selected unit and package before committing.

Start with how your team works

Write down who will attend, when they will be present and which activities need private rooms. Include calls, visitors, confidential meetings, storage, equipment and accessibility needs. Then decide which facilities must be exclusive to your team and which can be shared under agreed booking rules.

This brief is more useful than choosing a label first. A team with frequent private meetings needs to understand room availability and charges. A business with a specific layout needs to understand fit-out permissions and responsibilities in either format.

What the OnPoint listings actually advertise

On 19 October 2026, the OnPoint Office G.02 listing published an area of 172.66 m² and asking rate of R117.50 per m² per month. Its features include furniture options, three meeting rooms, private call booths, shared kitchens, reception, monthly tenant credits and four covered parking bays.

Those are advertised listing features. They do not confirm that all facilities are exclusive, that a particular furniture choice is included, that meeting use is unlimited, or that credits cover a given service. Ask for the package schedule, allocation, booking conditions and separate charges. The OnPoint package checklist sets out what to request.

What to check in a conventional office

Start with the current floor plan, existing fit-out and required work. For example, the Sunbird ground-floor listing publishes 500.66 m² at R120 per m² per month and describes ground-floor accommodation. It does not establish a complete furniture, connectivity, parking or backup package.

Ask who supplies and maintains the services your operation depends on. Request a written scope for fit-out, cabling, furniture and any changes before occupation. Confirm the proposed term, deposit/security, charge start dates and occupation programme instead of assuming conventional terms are fixed or serviced terms are flexible.

Compare the same workplace and cost basis

  • Workspace: can the actual layout support your attendance, meetings, equipment and privacy needs?
  • Services: which items are included, capped, bookable, metered or separately charged?
  • Control and responsibility: who approves changes, handles maintenance and manages access or service issues?
  • Timing: what is ready now, what work remains and when can the team occupy?
  • Cost: compare the full quote and initial cash requirement, using the office quote worksheet.

These two published examples differ in area and configuration, so their asking rates do not prove that either format is cheaper. No verified like-for-like total package comparison is established here.

View the options with one brief

Use the current serviced-office vacancies and conventional office vacancies, then confirm availability with leasing. Published photographs may show proposed works; inspect the actual space and agreed handover condition.

Discuss a serviced-office requirement, or request conventional office options. Bring the same team brief to both conversations.

title: OnPoint Serviced Offices: Your Package Checklist
seoDescription: Check furniture, meeting rooms, tenant credits, parking and service terms before choosing an OnPoint serviced office. View current units.
excerpt: Turn advertised OnPoint features into a written package schedule covering allowances, booking rules, services, charges and occupation timing.
contentHtml:
Before choosing a serviced office, turn the advertised feature list into a written package schedule. For each service, confirm the allocation, limits, operating arrangements and cost for your team. The word “serviced” does not answer those questions on its own.

Use this checklist with the OnPoint serviced-office guide and the specific live serviced-office listings. For a broader format comparison, read serviced versus conventional offices.

Confirm which suite and area are being quoted

The OnPoint Office G.07 listing, checked on 19 October 2026, publishes 124.49 m² at R117.50 per m² per month and “Immediately” availability. These are listing statements, not a final package quote or confirmed handover date.

Ask for the current plan, agreed rentable area and exact suite identity. Check the furniture layout against attendance, storage, accessibility and privacy needs. An area figure does not establish how many people can safely or practically work there.

Ask six package questions

  1. Furniture: the source advertises furnished or unfurnished options. Which items are supplied with this quote, in what condition and at what charge? Who handles changes or replacement?
  2. Meeting rooms and call booths: the source advertises three meeting rooms and private call booths. Confirm shared versus exclusive use, booking rules, included allowances, opening hours and any extra-use charges.
  3. Tenant credits: monthly tenant credits appear in the listing. Request the value, eligible services, expiry or carry-over rules and the charge once credits are used. No specific allowance is established by the feature label.
  4. Parking and access: the source lists four covered parking bays. Confirm the allocation to this suite, whether charges are included, visitor arrangements, access hours and any additional-bay options.
  5. Connectivity and backup: request the actual connectivity provision, support arrangements and any separate charges. Confirm which equipment and circuits have backup, capacity and operating limits; shared estate features do not establish this unit’s coverage.
  6. Shared facilities: the source lists kitchens, reception and an on-site barista. Confirm the current service, operating hours, allocation, permitted use and any charges rather than assuming unlimited inclusion.

Compare cost and responsibility together

Ask for base rent, VAT treatment, recoveries, utilities and every applicable service charge on the same schedule. Mark each line as included, separately priced, capped, metered, not applicable or awaiting confirmation. Keep deposit/security and setup spending separate from the recurring monthly total.

Record who deals with connectivity, furniture, access and maintenance issues. A service without an agreed scope or responsible contact can leave an operational question unresolved even if it appears in promotional copy.

Confirm readiness and the written terms

Agree the proposed term, occupation date, any required work, charge start dates and the process for changing your space or service use. Do not assume a serviced-office arrangement can be cancelled at any time or expanded on demand. Have the written terms reviewed by your own advisers where needed.

Use the office viewing checklist to inspect the suite, and the quote-comparison worksheet to compare it with another option. Package features and availability can change after this article’s source check.

Request the current OnPoint package schedule and a viewing. Include team attendance, meeting frequency, privacy needs, parking requirement and your target occupation date.

title: Office Viewing Checklist for Midrand Tenants
seoTitle: Office Viewing Checklist for Midrand Tenants
seoDescription: Plan an office viewing with checks for layout, access, parking, fit-out, connectivity and backup. Explore current Midpoint vacancies.
excerpt: Bring a clear team brief to your viewing and leave with confirmed unit information, documents and named actions for unresolved questions.
contentHtml:
A useful office viewing tests a particular unit against your working day. Bring a team brief and leave with a list of confirmed facts, missing documents and actions, rather than relying on the impression of a bright room or an advertised amenity.

Use this checklist alongside our offices to rent in Midrand guide and current office vacancies. If you need a serviced suite, also check the OnPoint guide and its package conditions.

Before the visit: send a short brief

Tell leasing your expected attendance, private-office and meeting-room needs, visitor volumes, parking requirement, critical equipment, target move date and budget. Include access or accessibility needs and any work that must happen before occupation.

Ask for the exact unit reference, current floor plan, published area, asking rate, availability and a list of existing versus proposed work. Confirm which entrance to use through the estate location page and your viewing contact. Do not treat gate access as evidence of staffed leasing or tenant operating hours.

Walk the daily route

  1. Arrival: check the intended entrance, parking allocation, visitor process and route to the office with the people who will use it.
  2. Working area: compare the actual layout with your attendance, storage, private calls and meeting needs. Note fixed features and obstructions that affect the plan.
  3. Building services: ask about connectivity, electrical provision, ventilation or cooling, water and support arrangements for this unit. Arrange appropriate technical checks for critical requirements.
  4. Backup: confirm the supported equipment/circuits, allocation and operating arrangements. A generator or backup-water label does not establish uninterrupted service to every tenant use.
  5. Fit-out and condition: record what exists, what is proposed, who will do the work and what must be agreed before handover.
  6. Costs and dates: request the complete quote, area basis, term and occupation programme. Record unresolved points rather than treating a verbal estimate as final.

Use the listing as a starting record

For example, Sunbird ground-floor office published 500.66 m², an asking rate of R120 per m² per month and immediate availability when checked on 19 October 2026. Its description identifies ground-floor accommodation and a minimum lease of 12 months. Confirm that the current offer and handover match those statements.

Unit 1, 1 Weaver Avenue is another published office option. Request its current plan and visit the specific suite rather than assuming its layout or service allocation matches Sunbird. Listing photographs may include proposed works and do not replace a condition check.

Leave with documents and named actions

Request the current dimensioned plan, confirmed rentable-area schedule, fit-out scope, specification/service schedule and complete written quote. Record who will resolve each outstanding item and by when. The floor-plan checklist helps assess the layout; the quote worksheet helps compare costs.

If you also inspect warehouse or conversion space, do not let that enquiry inherit office assumptions. The 2 Kingfisher area conflict remains unresolved at 3,849 versus 3,300 m²; obtain the approved schedule and plans before using an area or monthly-rent calculation.

Arrange the right viewing

Arrange an office viewing with your team brief, or request an OnPoint serviced-office viewing. Agree availability, required work and dates with leasing before planning a move.

title: Office Floor Plans and Fit-Out: A Midrand Checklist
seoTitle: Office Floor Plan and Fit-Out Checklist | Midrand
seoDescription: Test an office floor plan against your team, meetings, equipment and fit-out needs. Request current Midpoint plans, unit details and a viewing.
excerpt: Use a current unit plan to map activities, test practical constraints and agree the fit-out scope, responsibilities and occupation programme.
contentHtml:
Use an office floor plan to test how the space will work for your team before deciding how much fit-out it needs. Published area alone does not establish practical desk capacity, accessibility, approval requirements or the cost of adapting the unit.

This planning checklist supports our Midrand office guide. Use it after an initial shortlist and alongside the office viewing checklist.

Start with the correct plan and area basis

Request a current, dimensioned plan for the exact unit, identifying its revision/date and existing versus proposed layout. Match the unit reference and priced area to the written quote. Ask how rentable area is measured and whether any shared or ancillary area is included.

The Unit 2, 5 Weaver Avenue listing, checked on 19 October 2026, publishes 2,405 m² at R110 per m² per month and describes an open-plan layout with a private outdoor area. That is a listing description, not a verified fit-out drawing, workplace capacity or confirmation that alterations are approved.

Map activities before placing desks

List the work your team needs to do: focused tasks, calls, private conversations, collaboration, client meetings, storage, deliveries and equipment use. Record typical and peak attendance, then place those activities on the actual plan.

  • Workstations: test furniture dimensions and the required circulation without assuming a standard desk count from the advertised area.
  • Privacy and meetings: identify private rooms, noise-sensitive work, visitor waiting and routes that should not interrupt staff.
  • Support space: locate storage, equipment, staff facilities and any delivery or waste route your operation needs.
  • Fixed constraints: record columns, doors, stairs, service positions and features that cannot simply move with the furniture.
  • Access and safety: ask the appropriate qualified advisers to assess accessibility, circulation, fire/escape requirements and the approvals applicable to the proposed use and work.

A sketch is useful for a discussion, but it is not a certified capacity or compliance assessment. Confirm those requirements for the actual unit and proposed layout.

Turn the layout into a scope of work

Separate retained items from changes. List partitions, doors, furniture, cabling, connectivity, electrical work and any changes to building services. Confirm what the landlord provides, what the tenant supplies, who approves the design and which work requires specialist input.

Ask for cost, responsibility and timing beside each item. Include the dependencies: an occupation date is not credible if required design, approvals, installation or testing remain unresolved. Do not assume an advertised office is ready for your layout or that a contribution is available.

Check service allocation against the plan

Put critical equipment and connectivity needs on the drawing, then confirm the relevant supply and backup arrangements. Shared estate generator or backup-water features do not establish the allocation to your suite. Confirm supported equipment/circuits and current operating arrangements with leasing and the appropriate technical contacts.

If a serviced office is an alternative, test the actual suite and written package against the same activity map. The format comparison and OnPoint package checklist identify the service and booking questions that a floor plan cannot answer.

Connect the plan to the budget and live options

Use the office cost guide to separate fit-out spending from recurring costs, and request a quote for the agreed scope. Browse current office vacancies and the live office comparison for published options.

Request the current floor plan and an office viewing. Include your attendance pattern, activity list, parking needs, equipment and target move date so leasing can discuss the selected unit.
